paragraphs.text: “The [true] God.” Heb., ha·ʼElo·himʹ; Gr., The·ouʹ; Sy, “Jehovah.” See App 1F.
Lit., “he (one) had put,” M; many Heb. mss, “was there.”
“Hiram,” LXXSyVg, some Heb. mss and 1Ch 14:1; M, “Huram.”
“Our God.” Heb., ʼElo·hehʹnu, pl. of ʼElohʹah, to denote majesty and divine powers.
“The [other] gods.” Heb., ha·ʼelo·himʹ; Gr., the·ousʹ; Lat., deʹos.
“Food,” by a slight correction of M in agreement with TSyVg and 1Ki 5:11.
Or, “to Hiram my father.” Lit., “to Huram my father.” Heb., leChu·ramʹ ʼa·viʹ. Compare 4:16 ftn.
“That were alien residents.” Or, “the temporary residents.” Heb., hag·geh·rimʹ; LXXVg, “the proselytes.”
‘A cubit by the former measurement’ was possibly the same as the long cubit that equaled 51.8 cm (20.4 in.). See Eze 40:5 ftn, “Handbreadth.”
“A hundred and twenty,” MLXXB; LXXASy, “twenty cubits.” By a transposition of the letters of the Heb. word for “a hundred” it would read “cubits,” to produce the expression “twenty cubits.”
Or, “studded the house with precious stones.”
“In necklace style,” by a slight correction; M, “in the innermost room.”
“Gourd-shaped ornaments,” by a correction in agreement with 1Ki 7:24. Lit., “bulls.”
About 66,000 L (17,430 gal) when filled to capacity. Compare 1Ki 7:26 ftn, “Measures.”
“Upon the pillars,” LXX; M, “in front of the pillars.”
Lit., “the thickness (compactness) of the ground,” that is, the clayey ground. Possibly, by a correction of M, “at the ford of Adamah.” See 1Ki 7:46 ftn, “Mold.”
“The priests the Levites,” M; TLXXSy and 24 Heb. mss, “The priests and the Levites”; Vg, “The priests with the Levites.”
“Holy,” LXX, five Heb. mss and 1Ki 8:8; M, “Ark.”
“They,” TLXXSy, many Heb. mss and 1Ki 8:8; M, “it.”
“To time indefinite.” Lit., “times indefinite.” Heb., ʽoh·la·mimʹ, pl.
“God.” Heb., ʼElo·himʹ; Gr., The·osʹ; Lat., Deʹus.
Or, “cities,” as represented by their gates.
“Your anointed one.” Lit., “your anointed ones.” Heb., meshi·cheyʹkha, pl.; Gr., khri·stouʹ; Syr., dam·shi·chakh; Lat., chriʹsti.
“Congregation.” Heb., qa·halʹ; Gr., ek·kle·siʹa; Lat., ec·cleʹsi·a.
“The man of the [true] God.” Heb., ʼish-ha·ʼElo·himʹ. See App 1F.
Or, “the traffickers.” Possibly, by a correction of M, “the ships of Tarshish.”

“To your gods.” Lit., “to your tents.” Heb., leʼo·ha·leyʹkha. One of the Eighteen Emendations of the Sopherim. The original Heb. text is alleged to have read leʼ·lo·heyʹkha (from ʼelo·himʹ, “gods” or “God”), but by transposing l and h, the second and third consonants of the Heb. word ʼelo·himʹ, the Sopherim made M read “tents.” See App 2B.
“Goat-shaped demons.” Perhaps to those worshiping them these were thought to be hairy creatures having the form of a he-goat. See Le 17:7 ftn, “Demons.”
“His lord.” Heb., ʼadho·navʹ, pl. of ʼa·dhohnʹ, to denote excellence.
“As gods.” Or, “as god.” Heb., leʼ·lo·himʹ, pl. of ʼelohʹah. See 1Ki 12:28 ftn, “God.”
“A young bull.” Lit., “a bull, a son of a herd.”
“Of what are no gods.” Heb., leloʼʹ ʼelo·himʹ.
Or, “commentary; midrash.” The first of two occurrences of “midrash” in M. See 24:27 and ftn.
Lit., “in front of him,” M; Gr., eis sy·nanʹte·sin au·toiʹ; Vgc(Lat.), obʹvi·am eʹi. Compare Ge 10:9 ftn, “Opposition to.”
“Mortal man.” Heb., ʼenohshʹ; Gr., anʹthro·pos; Lat., hoʹmo.
“Now for Azariah.” Heb., wa·ʽAzar·yaʹhu, meaning “Jehovah Has Helped.”
Or, “a God of truth (faithfulness).” Heb., ʼElo·hehʹ ʼemethʹ.
Or, “and the temporary residents.” Heb., wehag·ga·rimʹ; Gr., pro·se·lyʹtous, “proselytes.”
“And with horns (shofars).” Heb., u·veshoh·pha·rohthʹ, animals’ curved horns.
“In his grand burial place.” Lit., “in his burial places.” Heb., veqiv·ro·thavʹ, pl. to denote excellence; LXX, “tomb”; Vg, “sepulcher.”
Not a cremation of Asa but a burning of spices.
Heb., Mi·khaʹyehu. See Mic Title ftn.
“There will be a disguising and entering,” that is, on Ahab’s part. In Heb. these are verbs, understood to be in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
“The legal cases of the inhabitants of Jerusalem,” by a correction of M and in agreement with LXXVg; M, “the legal case. Then they returned to Jerusalem.”
Lit., “between blood and blood.” Compare De 17:8.
“The chief priest.” Lat., sa·cerʹdos et ponʹti·fex.
Lit., “from the Ammonim.” Heb., me·ha·ʽAm·moh·nimʹ; by a transposition of letters in M, “the Meunim; Meunites”; LXX, “the Minaians”; Vgc, “the Ammonites.”
“From Edom,” one Heb. ms; Heb., me·ʼAramʹ, “from Syria”; Gr., Sy·riʹas; Lat., Syʹri·a; Sy, “the Red Sea.”
“In the congregation of.” Heb., biq·halʹ; Gr., ek·kle·siʹai.
“Clothing,” Vg and seven Heb. mss; M, “carcasses.”
“Israel,” M(Heb., Yis·ra·ʼelʹ)Vg; LXXSyVgc and about 40 Heb. mss, “Judah.”
“From Elijah.” Heb., me·ʼE·li·yaʹhu; the only mention of Elijah in Chronicles. See 1Ki 17:1 ftn, “Elijah.”
“Ahaziah.” Heb., ʼAchaz·yaʹhu. The same as “Jehoahaz” in 21:17, also meaning “Jehovah Has Taken Hold.” Here God’s name, abbreviated as Yaʹhu, follows “Ahaz” instead of preceding it.
“As for Azariah.” Heb., wa·ʽAzar·yaʹhu; in vss 1, 2, 7-11, “Ahaziah.”
“The priests and the Levites,” LXXSyVg and some Heb. mss; M, “the priests, the Levites.”
“Servant of the [true] God.” Heb., ʽe·vedh-ha·ʼElo·himʹ; Sy, “servant of Jehovah.” See App 1F.
“Sons,” MSy; LXXVg, “son.” Possibly M uses the pl. here to denote the excellence and worth of Jehoiada’s son Zechariah, the prophet-priest.
Or, “midrash.” Heb., midh·rashʹ. The only other occurrence of this Heb. word in M is in 13:22, where see ftn.
Meaning “My Strength Is Jehovah.” Heb., ʽUz·zi·yaʹhu.
Or, “the high priest.” LXX, “the first priest”; Lat., ponʹti·fex.
A cor equaled 220 L (200 dry qt).
“In the valley of the son of Hinnom.” Heb., beghehʼʹ ven-Hin·nomʹ; Gr., en Gai·be·ne·nomʹ; Vgc(Lat.), in valʹle Be·nenʹnom. See App 4C.
“Israel,” M; TLXXSyVg and about 12 Heb. mss, “Judah.”
“There was an acting with . . . unfaithfulness.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.

“Unfaithfulness,” M; Gr., a·po·sta·siʹai, “apostasy,” from the verb a·phiʹste·mi, “stand away from”; the noun has the sense of desertion, abandonment or rebellion. See Jos 22:22; Ac 21:21; 2Th 2:3 ftns.
“The congregation.” Heb., haq·qa·halʹ; Gr., he ek·kle·siʹa.
Lit., “voice.” Heb., qohl; Gr., keʹryg·ma, “proclamation; preaching.” Compare Mt 12:41 ftn.
“The man of the [true] God.” Heb., ʼish-ha·ʼElo·himʹ.
Or, “and the temporary residents.” Heb., wehag·ge·rimʹ; LXXVg, “proselytes.”

“Blessed his people, and we still have this quantity (great number; multitude) left,” LXX. This difficult passage in M appears to read: “blessed his people and the remainder (ones left over), even this crowd.”
“And Jeshua.” Heb., weYe·shuʹaʽ; LXX, “Jesus.” See Ge 49:18 ftn, “You.”
Lit., “not any god.” Heb., loʼ . . . kol-ʼelohʹah, sing. of ʼelo·himʹ.
“Deliver,” pl. in Heb., in agreement with its subject ʼElo·heh·khemʹ, “your own God,” which is pl. to denote majesty and divine powers. The verb in LXXVg is sing.; likewise in M, vs 17b.
“And Isaiah.” Heb., wI·sha·ʽeyaʹhu, meaning “Salvation of Jehovah”; LXX, “Esaias”; Vgc, “Isaias.”
“His god.” Heb., ʼelo·havʹ, pl. of ʼelohʹah, applied to the false god of Sennacherib to denote majesty; Gr., the·ouʹ; Lat., deʹi.
Meaning “My Portion Is Jehovah.” Heb., Chil·qi·yaʹhu.
“The inhabitants of Jerusalem,” MTLXXSyVg; Mmargin and many Heb. mss, “they returned to Jerusalem.”
“Doers,” LXXSyVg and many Heb. mss; M, “doer.”
“The blood from their hand,” LXX; Sy, “some of the blood.”
Lit., “What [is there] to me and to you?” A Heb. idiom; a repellent question indicating objection to Josiah’s intervention. See App 7B.
“Not against you that I am coming today,” LXXSyVg; M, “not against you yourself today.”
“In his palace.” Heb., beheh·kha·lohʹ; LXXVg, “in his temple.”
Lit., “rising up early and sending.” In Heb. these are verbs in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
“Of Cyrus.” Heb., leKhohʹresh; Gr., Kyʹrou; Syr., leKu·resh; Lat., Cyʹri.
“The God of the heavens.” This expression also occurs in Ge 24:3, 7; Ezr 1:2; Ne 1:4, 5; Ne 2:4, 20; Jon 1:9.
